title: Edit size separates the never-caught row, and nothing else
caption: One dot per backdoor, all 500. Across is lines changed, up is how many of seven monitors caught it at a 2% budget, spread vertically so dots do not stack. The bottom row, caught by nobody, has a median of 11 changed lines against 26 for the top row.
notes: The relationship is not a gradient. Median edit size by row runs 11, 25, 33, 31, 23, 29, 19, 26, so only the bottom row stands apart. Backdoors are close to all or nothing: 49 are caught by none and 277 by all seven, leaving 174 split across the six rows in between.
Read as an attacker's guide this says the small edit is the one worth making: 32% of edits of five lines or fewer got past all seven monitors, against 4.4% of edits of fifty lines or more.
The x-axis is capped at 100 lines. 12 backdoors change more than that and are drawn on the cap line, so the right edge is a pile rather than a position.

This row count is the seven-monitor panel at a 2% budget. 49 backdoors scored no catches here, while the hard-backdoor set counts 41 as never caught, because that set also asks the wider 0 to 100 scale monitors, which find eight of these.
Rows are integers and the vertical spread is cosmetic jitter, seeded from the problem id so it is identical on every rebuild. Height within a row carries no meaning.

xAxis.name: Lines changed, honest to backdoor (capped at 100)

yAxis.name: Monitors that caught it, of seven
